rules.title: Return of security deposit within 30 days after broken lease (timing)
rules.requirement: When a tenant breaks the lease, the landlord's 30-day period to return the security deposit does not begin until the unit is re-rented or the lease expires, whichever occurs first.
rules.coverage_text: Tenancies where the tenant breaks the lease agreement.
rules.citation: Truth in Renting (NJ DCA) – security deposit return
rules.quoted_span: the 30 days that the landlord shall return the tenant’s security deposit does not start until the landlord re -rents the rental unit, or until the lease expires, whichever occurs first.
rules.key_value: 30 days from re-rental or lease expiry
rules.ambiguity_note: Chunk begins mid-sentence; no statute cited for this passage in this chunk.

rules.title: Deposit return when tenant displaced by fire, flood, condemnation or evacuation
rules.requirement: The landlord must return the security deposit within five business days after a tenant is displaced, and within three business days of notice must tell the tenant where to collect it.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants displaced by fire, flood, condemnation, or evacuation where an official posted a notice prohibiting occupancy or certified displacement will last longer than seven days.
rules.quoted_span: Within five (5) business days after a tenant is displaced by fire, flood, condemnation, or evacuation, the landlord must return the security deposit.

rules.title: New owner responsible for security deposit after sale or transfer
rules.requirement: On sale or transfer, the new owner must obtain the deposit and accrued interest from the former owner and is responsible for investing it, giving notices, paying interest and returning it.
rules.quoted_span: If the property is sold or transferred it is the duty of the new owner to obtain the security deposit, plus accrued interest on the tenant’s deposit, that was collected by the former owner.

rules.title: Civil penalty for withholding deposit of tenant receiving government assistance
rules.requirement: A landlord who willfully and intentionally withholds the security deposit of a tenant receiving State or federal financial assistance may face a civil penalty of $500 to $2,000 per offense; the tenant need not sue to stay in the program.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants who have received financial assistance through any State or federal program, including welfare or rental assistance.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord may be liable for a civil penalty of not less than $500 or not more than $2,000 for each offense.

rules.title: Criminal penalty for unlawful use of security deposit monies
rules.requirement: Unlawful use of security deposit monies is a disorderly-person offense punishable by a fine of at least $200 or up to 30 days imprisonment, or both.
rules.coverage_text: Any person who unlawfully uses security deposit monies.
rules.quoted_span: may be subject to a fine of not less than $200 or imprisonment for not more than 30 days, or both (N.J.S.A. 46:8-25).
rules.penalty: Disorderly person; fine of not less than $200 or up to 30 days imprisonment, or both

rules.title: Landlord may charge credit report cost and reasonable application fees
rules.requirement: A landlord may charge the tenant the cost of a credit report and may request reasonable rental application fees.
rules.coverage_text: Prospective tenants applying for rental housing.
rules.citation: Truth in Renting (NJ DCA) – Credit Checks and Background Checks
rules.quoted_span: The landlord is allowed to charge the tenant for the cost of the report. The landlord may also request reasonable rental application fees or employment verification.
rules.key_value: reasonable application fee; cost of report
rules.ambiguity_note: Summary guidance; no specific statute cited and no dollar cap stated.

rules.title: No statewide rent control; municipalities may adopt rent control
rules.requirement: New Jersey has no state law establishing or controlling rents; municipalities may adopt rent control or leveling ordinances. Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from local rent control for 30 years after completion.
rules.coverage_text: Local rent control is determined by municipal ordinance.

exemption_tests.description: Newly constructed multiple dwellings exempt from local rent control for 30 years following completion of construction.
Rents subsidized by governmental funding may also be exempt from local rent control.

rules.quoted_span: The State of New Jersey has no laws that establish, govern or control rents. Municipalities may pass an ordinance establishing rent control or rent leveling.
rules.key_value: No state cap; 30-year new construction exemption from local control

rules.title: No mid-lease rent increase; notice required to terminate lease and raise rent
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot raise rent mid-lease term; the old lease must be terminated with proper written notice and a new lease offered at the increased rent.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord cannot raise the rent mid-lease term.

rules.title: Rent increases must not be unconscionable
rules.requirement: Before evicting for nonpayment of an increased rent, the owner must serve a valid notice to quit and notice of rent increase; the increase must not be unconscionable and must comply with municipal rent ordinances.
rules.coverage_text: Residential tenancies subject to the Anti-Eviction Act.
rules.quoted_span: The increase in rent must not be unconscionable; it must not be so unreasonable as to shock the conscience of a fair and honest person and must comply with any municipal ordinances governing rent increases.

rules.title: No rent increase to cover conversion costs
rules.requirement: When a building is converted to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership, rents may not be increased to cover costs resulting solely from the conversion; increases for new services or amenities remain allowed.
rules.coverage_text: All tenants in buildings converted to condominium, cooperative, or fee simple ownership.
rules.quoted_span: If a building is converted to a condominium or cooperative form of ownership, or to fee simple ownership of units, rents may not be increased to cover cos ts resulting solely from the conversion
